tasks.title: Export subscription shapes, validators and shared retention constants
tasks.spec: ## Repository: contract, all behavior, checks and completion evidence; R1, R8 invariant wire answer, R10 shared link-life and cleanup constants, D13, Contract fields, Address rule counterexamples, Performance impact, applicable Security impact checks and Acceptance evidence items 3 and 5. Keep schemas, identity-preserving validators, exports, generated outputs and version in one cohesive additive change. Status and notify consume the merged full SHA; WIRE_VERSION stays 1.

acceptance.expected: 0 failing tests. Every Address rule counterexample has its literal result; local lengths 64/65 and total lengths 254/255 are checked. Validators preserve input identity, never throw, and reject missing/extra keys, wrong types and a 129-character token. Anchored flag-free token patterns reject length +/-1 and '+'. Constants equal 1024, 254, 86400000 and 3600000, and route/result literals match R1. Focused coverage can fail its gate; this check requires the test results, not exit 0. The wire subscribe answer is accepted for every valid normalized request; no membership-dependent result or 429 shape is introduced.

exit 0; lint, build, typecheck (including SubscriptionRequest, SubscriptionTokenRequest, SubscriptionAnswer and SubscriptionResult in test/types.fixture.ts), full tests and the 80% line coverage gate pass. Existing exports remain compatible, WIRE_VERSION is 1, and the package takes the next minor after main (2.5.0 after 2.4.0 or 2.4.1). Docs describe the invariant 202 accepted response and both retention constants.

acceptance.command: bun run build && git diff --exit-code -- dist
acceptance.expected: exit 0 after the generated dist changes have been committed; every emitted file, including the six listed outputs, matches source. Run the pinned CI install/lint/typecheck/build/dist/test sequence as specified in the section.

Per Performance impact, run five times on the starting main and five on the branch; report both median user+sys values and B - A in the PR, plus build_cpu_s per Performance impact. Branch test_cpu_s is no greater than the independent contract budget 9.0 s in api/bench/budgets.json; expected test/build increase is at most 0.2 s each.

Record build_cpu_s as user + sys and the starting-main versus branch comparison in the PR per Performance impact; expected increase is at most 0.2 s. The expected comparison comes from the spec, not from generated dist.

PR body records the version and merged full SHA for consumer pins, bun run check and dist consistency output, performance measurements, and applicable Security impact evidence: strict input validation, no new dependency, unchanged WIRE_VERSION.
